opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez (E046) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Requested write is within the full-time limit and at or below the requested level, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E046 is a contractor with basic training (note says full-time, but security record governs). Contractors max out at read without advanced training, so write to Payroll is not permitted. Recommend read.
reason: The Security record shows Daniel Gutierrez (E046) is a contractor with basic security training and states that the security record governs employment type over the HR note. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps the maximum at read. The requested write is above the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

- security training: basic

- recommendation: read

The policy says:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.
